review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/mcp_tools.go:393-404 (server state cached once per batch) and applyObservationSQL cap CTE :591-620; same in approveTool :781-788/:838 and approveToolSQL :908-915
review_defects.scenario: The gateway posts a 200-tool batch. lookupObservedServer reads the server as enabled at the start. While the batch is still running, an admin sends PATCH enabled=false or DELETE, and withMCPToolCascade switches every capabilities row of that server off. The writes still in flight, and every tool after that point in the batch, then run applyObservationSQL with d.enabled=true computed from the stale server snapshot. They set capabilities.enabled=true, availability_state='available' and a fresh health_checked_at. The CAS guard checks only capability_tools fields and never the server's current state. After hydration the gateway stops listing a deleted server, so nothing corrects the row until MCP_TOOL_OBSERVATION_TTL (1 h by default, up to 24 h). Until then the registry reports tools of a disabled or deleted server as callable. That breaks the patch comment's own claim that 'no tool row outlives the switch that turned its server off'. approveTool has the same race: it reads the server, a concurrent disable lands, then it writes enabled=callable.
review_defects.fix: Decide enabled inside the write statement against the server row as it is now. Add a CTE that takes SELECT ... FROM mcp_servers WHERE id=$6 AND (org_id=$1 OR org_id='global') AND deleted_at IS NULL FOR SHARE, and set enabled = $22 AND that row is enabled with rollout stable or canary. The cascade's UPDATE of mcp_servers then serializes with it. Do the same in approveToolSQL.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/registry_apis.go:1300-1305 (admin check skipped for scope=='user') with patch :1435-1474 (normalizeMCPConfig keeps AnnotationTrust when shared_with is widened) and the PUT carry-over CASE :1338-1343
review_defects.scenario: User A, not an admin, registers a user-scoped server with annotation_trust:true. This is allowed because s.Scope=='user'. Its tool delete_repo declares readOnlyHint:true and derives as class read (risk low, approval floor none). A then sends PATCH /api/v1/mcp/{id} {shared_with:[B,C]}. Only ownership is checked, and the stored annotation_trust survives because normalizeMCPConfig keeps the field. A later gateway write-through PUT, with the same endpoint and scope and no trust key, also carries it over. B's and C's runs now get delete_repo as a trusted read tool, decided by a non-admin. The handler's own comment says 'for a server shared beyond one user that takes an admin', and the trust is meant to be an admin call wherever others are exposed (DEC-12 D2 is still pending the owner).
review_defects.fix: Treat a user-scoped server with a non-empty shared_with as shared. Require verifiedIsAdmin to set or keep annotation_trust on it. In patch, clear AnnotationTrust (or refuse the change) when shared_with goes from empty to non-empty and the caller is not an admin. Gate the PUT carry-over the same way.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/mcp_tools.go:255-267 (default branch restores drifted to approved) with apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/capability_observation.rs:162-182 (per-replica ledger, 15 min refresh)
review_defects.scenario: There are two gateway replicas. The server changes echo_read from D1 to D2. Replica A's catalog refreshes and posts D2, the row goes to drifted with enabled=false, and A's ledger marks D2 as freshly posted. Replica B still holds D1 in its 60 s catalog cache, and its last post of the tool was more than 15 minutes ago, so the tool is due. B gets a listing and posts D1. decideObservation sees digest==pin with stored.state=drifted and qualifies, and sets the row back to approved and enabled. A will not post D2 again for 15 minutes, and B corrects it only on its next listing after its cache refreshes. So a stale observation lifts the quarantine on a tool whose server serves a changed definition, with no person involved. The plan row says the row stays disabled 'until approval'.
review_defects.fix: Do not let observation move a row out of drifted. Leave a drifted row drifted until approveTool, or a person's explicit restore, changes it. If automatic restore is wanted, carry the gateway's discovery timestamp and restore only when the observation is newer than the drift's observed_at.

review_defects.scenario: capability-core answers 200 for every per-tool outcome, including contended (three lost compare-and-sets) and rejected. post_observations treats any 2xx as success, so ledger.record(..., true) suppresses a re-post for REFRESH_INTERVAL (15 min). If a drift observation loses three races, for example with replicas posting at the same moment, it is reported as contended and dropped. The tool stays approved and enabled on the old pin for up to 15 minutes, although the gateway saw the change.
review_defects.fix: Parse the results array. Record each tool with a contended (or 5xx) outcome as failed so the 30 s back-off retries it, or have capability-core return a non-2xx status when any observation is contended.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/registry_apis.go:1347-1357 (registration cascade only when NOT $10 enabled)
review_defects.scenario: An admin re-registers a server with PUT, removing drop_all from tool_allowlist or setting rollout_state=quarantine while enabled stays true. The cascade does not run. The gateway filters by its new allowlist and never observes drop_all again. For a quarantined server it only re-posts after the 15 min ledger interval. The tool's capabilities row stays enabled and available until the observation TTL (1 h, up to 24 h) expires, and its capability_tools review_state stays approved.
review_defects.fix: In the registration statement, also cascade enabled=false to tool rows whose tool_name is not in the new allowlist, or whose server rollout_state is not stable or canary.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/availability.go:256-297 (tenant attestation path accepts kind=mcp_tool rows)
review_defects.scenario: A tenant health attester posts /api/v1/capabilities/availability for a cap.mcp_tool.* row at its current version (1.0.0-<pin12>). It refreshes health_checked_at, which keeps a tool the gateway no longer sees inside MCPToolObservationTTL indefinitely. It also overwrites availability_reason_code=tool_definition_changed on a drifted row, so the gate reports the generic capability_disabled instead of the drift cause. The observation window is supposed to be the whole health attestation of an MCP tool.
review_defects.fix: Refuse kind=mcp_tool rows in attestAvailabilityForLane: observation is their only attester.

review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:1830-1852 (observe only on gRPC ListMcpTools); apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/mcp_gateway.rs:50-58 (no credential, unstaged:false)

What was built. Proto: enum ReasoningEffort (REASONING_EFFORT_UNSPECIFIED..MAX = 0..6; values prefixed because proto enum values share the package scope), InferRequest.reasoning_effort = 17, ModelInfo.effort_levels = 8. Both are additive; field 13 stays a legacy input and the level wins.

inference-core grpc.rs: effort_from_wire maps the wire level to effort::Level (UNSPECIFIED to None; unknown numeric to invalid_argument), and From<ModelInfo> emits canonical lowercase names. The level is not erased from the legacy budget at the conversion; "level wins" is for the adapters' resolve.

Gateway thinking.rs is the single derivation. plan(profile, ceiling, ladder_on) returns a Plan {budget_tokens, effort, allowance_tokens}. Off, it is exactly the legacy budget_tokens (including the step-down). On, it is the level plus a budget of 0. source_review_plan(ladder_on) is 4096 off and High on. effort_level handles quick/brief to Low, deep/extended/thorough to High, canonical names pass through, and standard or empty to none. Unknown values go to none and bump gateway_effort_unknown_total with a warn. The metric is in thinking.rs, so gateway_metrics.rs is untouched. reasoning_allowance, raised_ceiling and allowance_for_wire mirror inference-core's allowance table and 32768 cap; the contract test allowance_table_matches_inference_core pins the copy by reading effort.rs. parse_ladder reads MODEL_GATEWAY_EFFORT_LADDER and only the literal "true" (trimmed) enables it.

Wired sites. The streamed turn (sse.rs) sets budget and reasoning_effort from thinking::plan. The ZDR turn goes through zdr_turn_settings_with, with ZdrTurnSettings.thinking: Plan carried into direct_infer_turn and the http_routes ZDR infer. Source validation calls source_review_plan and clears the level together with the budget for tool_reporting and for the private repair request. truncation_budget(cost_basis, allowance) now adds the allowance via raised_ceiling at both scoring sites; the fallback site derives it from grpc_req.reasoning_effort. /v1/models ModelDescriptor.effort_levels is skip_serializing_if empty, so the JSON is byte-identical while inference-core advertises nothing. notes:
Nothing was left over from an earlier attempt: git status showed the owned files untouched.

What was built:
- snapshot-throttle.ts adds createSnapshotWriter (the first call writes at once, calls in the next window collapse into one trailing write, flush/cancel/dispose, interval 0 writes every call), flushOnPageLifecycle (visibilitychange to hidden, pagehide) and parseSnapshotThrottleMs. Cadence is timer-driven, so it is exact under fake timers.
- In use-chat-controller.ts:
  - The persistence effect now calls snapshotWriter.schedule(threadId) instead of writeThreadSnapshot. The writer carries only the thread id and reads state.turns and state.taskSteps when it writes, so a late write is the latest state. A write for a thread no longer in view is dropped.
  - writeThreadSnapshot is unchanged, so the temporary, foreign-origin and retention guards run at write time. A pending write is dropped, not flushed, if the thread turns temporary or the org turns ZDR before the window closes.
  - Flush points: before loadThread, resetChatState, branchAt and a new-thread send mutate state; on page hidden and pagehide; and in cleanup before disposed is set. Terminal writes stay direct and synchronous.
  - upsertTaskStep returns early when the merged step equals the existing one, ignoring createdAt.
  - appendUiEvent keeps only the first message.delta per stream. The stream is keyed by assistant turn id, or `<id>:resume` for a resumed connection. resetUiEvents replaces setUiEvents at the five reset sites.
- I flipped the S1 pins in the stream-churn test (CRLF kept) to the S3 targets. The new snapshot-throttle controller test covers every trigger, ZDR and temporary at every trigger, the throttle=0 rollback, an invalid value falling back to the default, and the Trace and step behaviour.

Flag: VITE_CHAT_SNAPSHOT_THROTTLE_MS is parsed strictly (whole ms only, anything else keeps 1000, capped at 60000).

Known and accepted:
- A terminal write is followed, at most one window later, by one more write when the effect re-runs. I did not suppress it because it also persists post-terminal changes such as ratings and edits. The target of one write per terminal is therefore met as a synchronous, unthrottled terminal write plus at most one trailing write.
- A hard-killed tab loses up to 1 s of local-only partial text. The plan accepts this.
